references.role: Required extension icon files and version

conclusion: No new raster assets are needed. Retain the three existing Chrome extension icons; build every workspace visual in React, CSS, SVG, or Lucide.
qa_scope: Both reference images and all three retained icon files were visually inspected. Accepted semantic rows confirm the no-raster classification and handoff, not the fidelity of application code still under construction.

direct.strategy: Retain the existing standalone project asset unchanged for Chrome toolbar and manifest use.
Retain the existing standalone project asset unchanged for Chrome manifest use.
Retain the existing standalone project asset unchanged for Chrome manifest use.

implementation.components: React aside/nav, utility header, main and footer; real links or buttons for routes, source, demo, theme and Open LinkedIn.
implementation.css: Desktop sidebar and fluid content grid; white panels, restrained neutral dividers, 14px major corners and 8px controls. CSS owns all backgrounds, spacing, borders and state treatments.
implementation.vectors: Lucide navigation, external-link, calendar, chevron and theme icons, hidden from assistive technology when adjacent text supplies the label.
implementation.responsive: Replace the sidebar with a compact header and horizontal navigation on narrow screens. Stack panels without shrinking controls into a dashboard thumbnail.

semantic.notes: The mock's navy presentation surround and rounded outer image frame are not product UI. No shell or card screenshots may ship.

implementation.components: A reusable SignalMark component beside the live-text Signal wordmark.
implementation.css: Align three ascending bars on a common baseline. Apply the workspace accent through currentColor and set the wordmark in the chosen system sans.
implementation.vectors: Inline SVG rectangles or three CSS bars. Preserve the existing rising-bar silhouette; do not trace the invented wifi or wave marks.
implementation.responsive: Keep the glyph crisp at popup, sidebar and compact-header sizes; retain a readable accessible name.

semantic.notes: Existing toolbar PNGs keep their current artwork. Their green/charcoal palette does not override the approved blue workspace direction.

implementation.components: Semantic headings, paragraphs, labels, outputs and tabular numeric text.
implementation.css: Use a local humanist system-sans stack. Start near 30px page headings, 16px section headings, 14px body and 12px secondary text; use tabular numerals for data.
implementation.responsive: Allow heading and label wrapping; preserve readable type and control labels in the compact popup and narrow layouts.

semantic.notes: No font download, text raster, faux lettering image or bespoke font asset is required.

implementation.components: A dl or semantic metric group for reviewed, kept, filtered and estimated time saved.
implementation.css: One shared white strip with aligned values, labels and a visible estimation note; use restrained accent colors rather than separate decorative tiles.
implementation.vectors: Lucide message, check, filter and clock icons.
implementation.responsive: Use a two-column or stacked arrangement when four metrics no longer fit; keep explanatory text beside its metric.

semantic.notes: Calculate from real aggregate data. Example counts belong only to a clearly labeled preview; the mock is not a data source.

implementation.components: A figure with a live seven-day stacked bar chart, legend and textual values or accessible data table.
implementation.css: CSS owns the panel, spacing, axis labels and legend. Preserve the approved broad chart area beside the smaller threshold panel.
implementation.vectors: Responsive SVG rects, rules and labels or CSS bars driven by the same aggregate dataset. Scale segments and totals from actual values.
implementation.responsive: Use a fluid viewBox or grid, keep day labels legible and stack the threshold panel below on narrow screens.

semantic.notes: Do not trace inconsistent bar heights, bracket values or totals in the generated comp. No chart image is needed.

implementation.components: A labeled input type=range from 0 to 100, an output for the current threshold, and real buttons or radio inputs for presets.
implementation.css: CSS owns the blue filled track, neutral remainder, thumb, preset selection and visible focus. Link the displayed score and preview state to the same value.
implementation.vectors: Lucide edit, open or target icons only where the approved control benefits from them.
implementation.responsive: Make the range span its panel, keep a usable touch target and wrap preset controls without dropping their labels.

semantic.notes: Keyboard input and accessible current values must work. The companion mock informs the preview interaction, not a second visual identity.

implementation.components: A fieldset for collapse, hide, blur and score-only modes; labeled checkbox/switch inputs for filtering status and sponsored-post filtering.
implementation.css: CSS draws tracks, thumbs, selected mode borders and state feedback. Apply blur to example content only when that mode is active, never bake it into an image.
implementation.vectors: Lucide collapse, eye-off, list, pause and play icons; use a precise vector blur glyph if a matching library icon is unavailable.
implementation.responsive: Wrap the mode grid on narrow panels and preserve text labels and keyboard focus. Do not rely on icon shape or color alone.

semantic.notes: The blurred blot in the companion mock is a generated control defect, not a required bitmap.

implementation.components: A semantic list with category labels, percentages or counts, and data-driven progress bars.
implementation.css: Use label/bar/value columns, a neutral track and blue fill; CSS owns rounded bar ends and consistent row spacing.
implementation.vectors: Lucide category icons with visible text labels.
implementation.responsive: Move each bar below its label/value row when necessary; keep numeric text visible.

semantic.notes: Use the application's category names and totals. The graphic is a data display, not an illustration.

implementation.components: An ordered list of actual filtering reasons with associated counts.
implementation.css: Align rank, optional icon, label and count using a compact grid with neutral separators or whitespace.
implementation.vectors: Lucide reason icons where the reason has a clear equivalent; use text rather than inventing symbols.
implementation.responsive: Let reason labels wrap while counts remain aligned; stack beneath categories on narrow screens.

semantic.notes: Mock labels such as low engagement or political content are not evidence of implemented filtering rules.

implementation.components: Reuse or adapt the existing TagEditor with an input, a list of live-text tags and labeled remove buttons.
implementation.css: Wrap compact tags in a flexible container; CSS owns chip fill, border, padding and interaction states.
implementation.vectors: Lucide X or a small inline vector for removal.
implementation.responsive: Wrap long labels and avoid fixed widths; keep remove controls reachable by keyboard and touch.

semantic.notes: Tags are editable profile data, not artwork. They need no generated asset.

implementation.components: React article elements for explicitly fictional example posts, live score/status badges, expandable explanations and real Show post buttons.
implementation.css: Use white post panels and a pale explanation region. CSS owns score chips, kept/filtered states, dimension bars and collapse/hide/blur transitions.
implementation.vectors: Lucide check, arrow and explanation icons; draw dimension bars in CSS or SVG from the example score data.
implementation.responsive: Stack posts and controls, wrap titles, and collapse multi-column score details into labeled rows. Respect reduced motion.

semantic.notes: Neither inspected reference requires author portraits, photography or post thumbnails. Text-only examples are sufficient and must not imply access to the user's LinkedIn feed.

implementation.components: A semantic table or definition list for available aggregate data, with real labels, dates, counts and any existing local-data actions.
implementation.css: Use tabular numerals, aligned columns and light rules within the approved panel system. Keep utility buttons and file inputs as controls.
implementation.vectors: Lucide download, upload or delete icons only for actions the implementation supports.
implementation.responsive: Use labeled stacked rows or an explicitly scrollable table when necessary; never shrink an entire ledger image.

semantic.notes: This role is semantic by requirement and inherits the approved workspace grammar. It must not invent saved-article history or adopt the rejected third comp as its overall composition.

excluded_mock_defects: Presentation-only outer frame and navy backdrop.
Invented wifi or wave logos in place of the established ascending bars.
Unconditional claim that data never leaves the device; optional AI and sync can send data.
Fabricated version 1.2.0; the inspected package and manifest specify 1.0.0.
Inconsistent chart totals, segment values and plotted heights.
Reason/category labels unsupported by the product's actual data model.
Raster-looking blur decoration in a semantic mode control.
execution_order: No raster production or mock cropping.
Retain the existing Chrome icon pack and its generator.
Implement the listed semantic roles with the approved layout and shared component grammar.
Parent verifies rendered fidelity, responsive states, real data and accessibility.
assumptions: The user delegated the direction and reference approval, as recorded in PRODUCT.md and the surface brief.
Mock PNGs remain reference material and are not imported into the shipping interface.
Local system fonts and the installed lucide-react package cover type and standard icon needs.
No photo, portrait, illustration, texture, decorative background or screenshot asset is part of this redesign.
The three retained PNGs belong to Chrome extension packaging, not the workspace's semantic UI.
Production credentials and cloud configuration were not inspected.
